contracts.contract_plain_english: For every refinement index m>=0, the computed next iterate differs componentwise from the exact solution by at most (1+u) times the absolute inverse applied to the exact intermediate residual, plus u times the magnitude of the exact solution. This is an explicit forward-error bound for the rounded update and contains no norm or big-O term. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 second inequality and proof]

source_evidence.observation: The problem is Ax=b with n equations and n unknowns over a floating-point subset of the reals. Unit roundoff u is positive, nu <= .01, every floating-point operation mentioned is assumed well-defined, and absolute values and inequalities are componentwise.
The exact solution is x=A^{-1}b, so A is implicitly nonsingular; Gaussian elimination uses column pivoting.

The initial computed solution x_1 and corrections d_m are obtained by column-pivoted solves; x_{m+1} is the floating-point subtraction of d_m from x_m. The artificial initialization is x_0=0, r_0=-b, d_0=-x_1. Both single- and double-precision residual accumulation are considered.
